open_findings.summary: The operator Skill — the one document a Hermes agent is told to load before it touches any techtree_ tool — states unconditionally that this build cannot do the journey. Its 'What this build cannot do yet' section says Techtree Hello World stops before preparing a comparison because the starter Skill has not been chosen for this release, and that proposing a revision stops for the same reason. Its troubleshooting reference says the release coordinates have not been chosen, that it will not install Techtree, that it cannot prepare the guided introduction, and that there is nothing to fix locally. All of that is false of this candidate: both founder Skills are pinned by digest, the CLI installed, the introduction prepared, and both comparisons ran. An agent following its instructions faithfully tells the user the journey is impossible.
open_findings.why_the_guards_missed_it: The copy contract scans these surfaces for forbidden claims and required frames. Nothing encodes 'a claim about what this build cannot do must match whether the release has chosen its founder Skills'.

open_findings.summary: The pinned guide and the plugin README both tell the user, in advance, exactly what the install-time security scan will say: 'five findings in three families', and they enumerate all five. The scan actually reports six, in four families, and Hermes' own decision line says '6 findings'. The sixth is a HIGH privilege escalation on skills/operator/references/questions.md — the very document that explains the five. A user comparing the promise to the screen finds an unexplained HIGH finding at the moment they are being asked to trust the plugin.

The engine-verified state can never be reached. techtree setup and techtree engine verify both report the engine installed and verified, but a Climb's compatibility status is derived by a class that can only ever answer not_installed or installed_unverified. So climb list, climb show, climb inspect and demo prepare all warn 'The evaluation engine is installed but has not been checked since' forever, and all offer 'Check that the installed evaluation engine is intact' as the next step — a next action the user can never clear, on the main onboarding surface.

The guided introduction's session lives only in the memory of the Hermes process that created it. The first comparison takes about eleven minutes and the guide instructs a restart during onboarding, so an ordinary session end loses it. The run survives and recovers by run identifier exactly as the contract requires, but techtree_uplift_propose then refuses with demo_session_not_found and no repair, and the second half of the introduction becomes unreachable. Reproduced live. The store carries a seven-day expiry constant that never applies, which suggests persistence was intended.

Unless the caller passes channel: 'terminal', every plugin answer comes back in the bounded chat form, and the guided-revision proposal loses its request accounting, its draft digest and its provenance. Hermes documents no field the plugin can read (DOCUMENTED_CHANNEL_KEYS is empty), and the operator Skill never mentions the argument, so the default for an agent-driven call is the phone-shaped answer. Hit live: the proposal this journey received carried request_accounting: null.

The approval event both runs recorded carries draft_digest: null. The plugin reads it from data.draft_digest on the start envelope and the CLI does not put one there. That is the single field that makes 'a person approved this exact draft' checkable.

The published install command on techtree.sh/start is 'uv tool install techtree==0.0.0-placeholder', with no --python. The same page's prose promises 'the installer provides its own Python 3.12, whatever this machine has'. Only the plugin's generated plan actually names it. This is WP11e's techtree-python-vom surviving on the website surface.

techtree run status prints 'Progress  not started' while the table immediately below it shows episodes completing on both sides. The top-level progress field is never populated during running_variants.
The second comparison's result payload reports task_count: null, where the first reported 36. The reader of Iteration 2 is not told how many tasks it ran.

The plugin's CLI-install result is the only successful response with no machine-readable next_action; its next step exists only as a sentence at the end of a message. Two typed refusals — techtree_climb_prepare's missing-argument error and demo_session_not_found — carry no repair at all.
dist/ carries no .sha256 sidecar beside the wheel, so a participant has nothing local to check a download against. The digest is recorded only in release/plugin-release-candidate.json.

The published plugin install command ends in --enable, which skips the 'Enable techtree now?' confirmation. The install-anyway approval still fires, so no stop condition is met, but the guide's own command pre-answers one of the two questions a user would otherwise be asked.

verdict_detail: Every approval gate the contract names held: nothing installed without a person answering for it, no surfaced command carried a floating coordinate, the paid Hello World comparison reproduced the certified science exactly and its proof verified offline, the one guided revision completed end to end for the first time in this programme, and the second comparison ran on its own separate approval. What does not hold is what happens before any of that. The operator Skill — the one document a Hermes agent loads before it touches a Techtree tool — states unconditionally that this build stops before preparing a comparison and that its release coordinates have not been chosen. Both are false of this candidate, and an agent that believes them abandons the journey in its first reply.
